# Evaluating ∫ 2*exp(x)*cos(x) dx

## Setting Up Integration by Parts

Let me first compute J = ∫ exp(x)*cos(x) dx, then multiply by 2.

**First integration by parts:**
- u = cos(x), dv = exp(x) dx
- du = -sin(x) dx, v = exp(x)

$$J = \exp(x)\cos(x) + \int \exp(x)\sin(x)\, dx$$

**Second integration by parts** (on ∫ exp(x)*sin(x) dx):
- u = sin(x), dv = exp(x) dx
- du = cos(x) dx, v = exp(x)

$$\int \exp(x)\sin(x)\, dx = \exp(x)\sin(x) - \int \exp(x)\cos(x)\, dx = \exp(x)\sin(x) - J$$

## Solving for J

Substituting back:

$$J = \exp(x)\cos(x) + \exp(x)\sin(x) - J$$

$$2*J = \exp(x)\cos(x) + \exp(x)\sin(x)$$

$$J = \frac{\exp(x)*\cos(x) + \exp(x)*\sin(x)}{2}$$

## Final Result

$$\int 2*\exp(x)*\cos(x)\, dx = 2*J = \exp(x)*\cos(x) + \exp(x)*\sin(x) + C$$

## Verification

$$\frac{d}{dx}[\exp(x)*\cos(x) + \exp(x)*\sin(x)]$$
$$= \exp(x)*\cos(x) + \exp(x)*(-\sin(x)) + \exp(x)*\sin(x) + \exp(x)*\cos(x)$$
$$= 2*\exp(x)*\cos(x) \checkmark$$

<answer>exp(x)*cos(x) + exp(x)*sin(x) + C</answer>
